title: Translation invariance of the affine-space trace over a Noetherian base
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible, where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $d\geq0$, put $V=\mathbf A^d_S$ with projection $q:V\to S$ [def-sbc-affine-space], and work in the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the ordinary finite Tate sheaves $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$, their twists and pullback identifications [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Put $L=A_V(d)[2d]$ and let $t_q:Rq_!L\to A_S$ be the explicit coordinate-tower counit trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with ordinary etale compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

For a section $a:S\to\mathbf A^d_S$ of $q$, that is $a=(a_1,\dots,a_d)\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)^d$, let $\tau_a:V\to V$ be the $S$-automorphism $z\mapsto z-a$. For the Cartesian square with both vertical maps $q$, bottom map $1_S$ and top map $\tau_a$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_{\tau_a}:Rq_!L\to Rq_!\tau_a^*L$ be the compact-support exchange of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and let $\kappa_a:\tau_a^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ be the Tate pullback identification. Then $$t_q\circ Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{\tau_a}=t_q.$$ The case $d=0$ is included, where $\tau_a$ is the identity.

source.place: Step 1: translation (the translation vector varying over the bundle, locally constant unit multiplier equal to 1 on the zero section, connected geometric fibres); ordinary-etale Noetherian-base, finite-ring formulation

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf A^d_S$, write $r:P\to S$, and form $W=\mathbf A^d_P=V\times_SP$ with projection $q_P:W\to P$. The coordinate-tower description [def-amb-affine-trace-tower] gives Noetherian schemes $P,W$, separated finite-type projections, and preservation of invertibility of $N$. Thus the same $N,A,d$ satisfy the trace hypotheses over $P$. Choose a compactification of $q_P$ by [thm-nagata-noetherian]. Its proper part is finite type over the Noetherian scheme $P$, hence its source is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the minimal condition on closed subsets [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] makes its topology Noetherian, and its open part is quasi-compact since all subsets of a Noetherian space are quasi-compact [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]. This is an allowed compactification for the action lemma. The universal translation $\tau_P(z,b)=(z-b,b)$ has inverse $(z,b)\mapsto(z+b,b)$; both formulas glue since each coordinate is a global coordinate over $P$.

source.place: Step 1: translation, sentences 1-4; parameter space for the translation vector and hypotheses for compact supports

proof.text: Let $L_P=A_W(d)[2d]$. It is a shifted sheaf, hence bounded below, and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] supplies $\kappa_P:\tau_P^*L_P\simeq L_P$. Apply [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] to obtain the automorphism $\rho_P=Rq_{P!}(\kappa_P)\circ E_{\tau_P}(L_P)$, its identity normalization, and its base-change equation. On this bounded-below input [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identifies these exchanges and compactification comparisons with precisely the unbounded exchanges of the statement. By [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] the specified coordinate-tower trace $t_P:Rq_{P!}L_P\xrightarrow{\sim}A_P$ is invertible. For every Noetherian $T$ and $u:T\to P$, write $C_u:u^*Rq_{P!}L_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{T!}L_T$. The two actual-map equations are $C_u\circ u^*\rho_P=\rho_T\circ C_u$ and $t_T\circ C_u=u^*t_P$. The Tate composition compatibility ensures that $\rho_T$ uses the canonical Tate identification after base change.

source.place: Step 1: translation, sentences 3-4; action on the trace and its comparison under specialization

proof.text: Conjugate the action to $\alpha=t_P\circ\rho_P\circ t_P^{-1}:A_P[0]\to A_P[0]$. Full faithfulness [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies this with a unique module-sheaf automorphism $\alpha_0:A_P\to A_P$. It is multiplication by $b=\alpha_0(1)\in A_P(P)$: for an etale object $U\to P$ and $c\in A_P(U)$, module linearity gives $\alpha_{0,U}(c)=c\alpha_{0,U}(1)=c\,b|_U$. The inverse map similarly gives a section $c$ with $bc=1$, so $b$ is a unit section, also when $A$ is the zero ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], $b$ is a Zariski-locally constant $A$-valued function on $|P|$. Moreover the equations of step 2 give $\alpha_T=u^*\alpha$, since $\alpha_T=t_TC_u(u^*\rho_P)C_u^{-1}t_T^{-1}=u^*(t_P\rho_Pt_P^{-1})$. Thus the scalar pulls back to the scalar for the specialized translation.

source.place: Step 1: translation, sentence 4: multiplication by a section of the locally constant sheaf of units

proof.text: For $s\in S$, let $K=\kappa(s)$ and consider $P_s=\mathbf A^d_K$. Its coordinate ring $K[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ is a nonzero integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], the zero prime has closure $V(0)=P_s$. Consequently every nonempty open contains that prime, so two disjoint nonempty opens cannot cover $P_s$: it is nonempty and connected. This includes $d=0$, when the ring is $K$. The restriction of the locally constant function $b$ to this fibre is constant by [lem-weil-pbc-connected-locally-constant-map]. Along the zero section $e:S\to P$ the specialized translation is the identity and its Tate identification is the identity; hence the identity normalization [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change], the Tate identity compatibility [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and step 3 give $e^*b=1$. Each fibre therefore has constant value $1$. Ordinary residue-field fibres suffice here: every point of $P$ over $s$ is the image of a point of $P_s$ (on affine charts the prime defining that point is disjoint from the denominators in $\kappa(s)$). Hence $b=1$ as a function, and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] gives $b=1$ as a section. Thus $\alpha=1$ and $t_P\rho_P=t_P$.

source.place: Step 1: translation, sentences 5-6: the multiplier is one on each connected fibre

proof.text:
Pull $t_P\rho_P=t_P$ back along the given section $a:S\to P$. Under the coordinate identification $W\times_{P,a}S=V$, the base change of $\tau_P$ is exactly $\tau_a(z)=z-a$. The Tate identity and composition compatibilities [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identify the specialized coefficient map with $\kappa_a$. Set $\rho_a=Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{\tau_a}$, using [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] to identify the bounded-below exchange with the stated one. The action equation [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] and trace equation [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] give
$$t_q\rho_a C_a=t_q C_a a^*\rho_P=a^*t_P\,a^*\rho_P=a^*(t_P\rho_P)=a^*t_P=t_q C_a.$$
Cancel the isomorphism $C_a$ to obtain the required equality. When $d=0$, $P=S$ and $\tau_a=1$, so the same computation is the identity normalization; when $S$ is empty it is the unique equality of the indicated maps.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-ba8fcba3f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of it: the item's five steps, the full statement of every cited node (including the blueprint_update texts for thm-nagata-noetherian, def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-pc-scheme and def-sbc-affine-space), and the source, main-20261015 sk-prop-sp-orientation-vector-bundle.proof.md Step 1. Statement, stmt_deps, blueprint, chapter, unit and created are byte-identical to the side-DAG base; only the proof fields, split_report and searches were added, so nothing was weakened. Step 1: def-amb-affine-trace-tower gives the Noetherian, separated finite-type and N-invertible hypotheses over P. Nagata gives a compactification, and def-nagata-compactification already makes its open immersion quasi-compact (the worker's extra quasi-compactness argument is also correct). Step 2: L_P is a shifted locally free sheaf, so it lies in D^+. The action lemma supplies the automorphism, its identity normalization and the actual-map base-change equation. Tate composition coherence makes the base-changed coefficient map the canonical one. The unbounded comparison lemma restricts to the thm-cbc-finite-torsion exchange that both the action and trace lemmas use. The trace lemma gives that t_P is invertible and that t_T C_u = u^*t_P. Step 3: full faithfulness for Mod(A_P) and linearity give multiplication by a section b, and the constant-sheaf lemma turns b into a Zariski-locally constant function. That pullback of such a section is composition with the map is left implicit, but it is a two-line local fact. Step 4: A^d_K is a nonempty domain spectrum, hence connected; b is 1 on the zero section by the identity normalization; residue-field fibres cover P (the affine-chart prime argument is correct); so b = 1. Step 5: base change along a gives exactly z -> z-a, and I checked each equality in the chain before cancelling the isomorphism C_a. Edge cases d=0, a=0, S empty and A=0 all hold. Duplicates: lem-pur-affine-translation-trace states the same equality only for separated finite-type schemes over k with A_{E,n}, so it is strictly narrower and the parent needs the Noetherian, finite-ring form. No other node states this. There is no cycle and no SGA citation. Every cited statement node lies on the transitive route of sk-i-curve-zero; the one exception is the Mathlib leaf lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets. The five declared tool_uses are all generic black boxes, so I accept them, although they are redundant. No new nodes and no fixes.

lean.statement: theorem ambientAffineTranslationTrace (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (hA : (N : A) = 0) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S] (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤))) (d : ℕ) (a : Fin d → Γ(S, ⊤)) : ambientAffineTranslationExchange A S d a ((affineTraceRight A N hA S d).obj (ordinaryFiniteUnit A S)) ≫ (affineTraceLeft A S d).map (ambientAffineTranslationTate A N hA (ambientAffineTraceTransport N hN A hA) S hS d a).hom ≫ affineTraceCounit A N hA (ambientAffineTraceTransport N hN A hA) (ambientAffineTraceDatum N hN A hA) S hS d = affineTraceCounit A N hA (ambientAffineTraceTransport N hN A hA) (ambientAffineTraceDatum N hN A hA) S hS d
lean.note: Uses the recorded coordinate-tower model of affine space, its shifted Tate object, and its actual counit. The translation, exchange, and Tate identification are explicit recursive composites, never arbitrary map binders. Normalized roots/pure-tensor transport and normalized projective-line Kummer data are selected from the dependency theorem; their normalization determines the maps used here. The line-square helper states the coordinate restriction of the Cartesian translation squares in this node.
